title: The Compass of the Sepik Basin
premise: Rafael Brightwater, a desert ranger who has spent a decade chasing petty thieves across empty miles, follows one such thief to the Sepik Basin, where an anomalous tide exposes a cave said to hold the ledger of a colonial-era magistrate who vanished with a fortune and a list of everyone he ever bought. The cave's map is real, but so is the thief's employer: a mining consortium's fixer who intends to buy the region's water rights using proof that the old magistrate forged every land deed in the basin. Trapped by monsoon season with a leaking boat and Ilse Marchetti, a hydrologist who knows what the documents mean for the river people, Rafael must choose between returning the ledger to the authorities who will bury it and delivering it to the villages whose justice was never written into law. The story ends with Rafael burning his ranger's commission, giving the ledger to the river councils, and staying through the flood—not as a man measuring miles, but as someone who has finally stopped running.
about_author: Sable Vasquez is a former river surveyor who spent six years documenting oral histories along remote tributaries before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels in which landscapes are characters and justice is something people build by hand.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Miles
chapters.summary: Rafael Brightwater's POV. In the desert outside Port Moresby's reach, Rafael tracks a thief named Corben Voss who stole not money but a sealed tube of old survey papers. Rafael measures his life in miles logged; the pursuit is routine until he realizes Voss is heading for the coast, toward water Rafael has avoided for ten years. Beat: restless competence masking avoidance.

chapters.title: The Tide That Lied
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. At a fishing village on the coast, an unprecedented low tide exposes a sea cave locals refuse to name. Inside, Rafael finds Voss's abandoned camp and a fragment of a chart referencing 'the Magistrate's Ledger.' A village elder warns him: the cave opens once a generation, and it always costs someone. Beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: A Stranger With Instruments
chapters.summary: Ilse Marchetti's POV. Hydrologist Ilse arrives measuring salinity anomalies, convinced the tide shift signals upstream tampering—someone diverting the basin's rivers. She and Rafael collide over the same boat, the only seaworthy one left before monsoon. Their friction is immediate and electric. Beat: two loners forced into proximity.

chapters.title: Upstream Against the Season
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. They push upriver ahead of the storm wall, Rafael tracking Voss's trail while Ilse logs water levels that make no sense. The boat begins leaking at the seams. First ambush: men in unmarked boats search the banks for them specifically. Beat: the chase becomes being chased.

chapters.title: The Fixer's Offer
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Captured briefly by agents of the Meridian Consortium, Ilse meets Dain Kessler, the fixer, who offers her funding for life if she stops asking questions about flow rates. He mentions Rafael by name—and by history. Ilse pretends to consider. Beat: temptation dressed as rescue.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A night in a stilt village reveals the human stakes: families whose land titles were declared void decades ago, now facing Kessler's purchase contracts. An old woman recites from memory the boundaries the paper erased. Rafael recognizes the shape of erased records—it mirrors a file from his own past. Beat: empathy ignites purpose.

chapters.title: Leaking Toward the Source
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The boat fails in rapids; they lose most supplies and wash ashore near the cave's inland entrance marked on the chart fragment. Soaked, exhausted, they argue about whether to go in or turn back. Ilse accuses Rafael of hiding from something. He doesn't deny it. Beat: intimacy through crisis.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Ledger
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Inside the cave: the preserved records of Magistrate Aldous Crane, who documented every bribe, forged deed, and bought verdict of the colonial administration—including the founding charter of the company that became Meridian. Rafael understands why Voss stole the survey tube: it's the key to reading the ledger's cipher. Beat: revelation with weight.

chapters.title: Voss, Cornered
chapters.summary: Voss's POV (first time). Corben Voss is found half-dead, betrayed by Kessler after delivering the tube. He confesses he never intended to sell the ledger—he wanted to give it back to the river people, as his grandmother was one of those dispossessed. He begs Rafael to finish what he started. Beat: enemy becomes mirror.

chapters.title: The Monsoon Arrives
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The storm hits. Rivers rise twenty feet in a day; the cave entrance floods; escape routes vanish. Kessler's men sweep the basin knowing the trio is trapped inside it. Ilse realizes the diverted flows aren't just for mining—they're engineered to drown the villages' claims, literally washing away boundary markers. Beat: nature and conspiracy converge.

chapters.title: Duty's Weight
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael radios his ranger command, reporting the find as protocol demands. Command orders him to secure the ledger for federal custody—custody Kessler demonstrably owns. Holding the radio, Rafael hears his own decade of obedience collapse into a single question: whose law is this? Beat: the theme made explicit.

chapters.title: Between the Pages
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Hiding in a flooded church ruin, Rafael and Ilse read the ledger through the night, translating Crane's cipher with Voss's tube. Between entries, they trade their own confessions—her disgraced career, his brother's death in a rigged water dispute. Love arrives quietly, between pages. Beat: tenderness under threat.

chapters.title: Kessler Closes In
chapters.summary: Kessler's POV (only chapter). Dain Kessler, once an idealist who believed development could be honest, rationalizes everything: the drownings will be accidents, the ledger a forgery, the deaths regrettable. His self-justification is chillingly reasonable. He orders the church ruins searched. Beat: corruption shown from inside.

chapters.title: The Betrayal at Wagu Bend
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A village guide offers to ferry them downstream—but sells them out to Kessler's men for his family's debt forgiveness. Ambush at Wagu Bend; Voss takes a bullet shielding the ledger. They escape into flooded forest, carrying a dying man and a book worth killing for. Beat: trust broken, cost counted.

chapters.title: Voss's Last Mile
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Voss dies at dawn in the mangroves, making Rafael promise the ledger reaches the river councils, not the courts. Ilse performs the burial rites she learned from these very villages years ago. Rafael, who has buried strangers for a decade, finally grieves one properly. Beat: grief transmuted into vow.

chapters.title: The Council of the Nine Tributaries
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Reaching the high-ground council house where nine river communities shelter from the flood, Rafael and Ilse present the ledger. The elders debate: some want it published, some fear reprisal, one wants it destroyed. Rafael argues for the dangerous middle path—use it, don't worship it. Beat: justice as collective decision.

chapters.title: Flood War
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Kessler's men attempt to seize the council house during peak flood, using the rising water as cover. Rafael, Ilse, and villagers defend it with knowledge of the channels—the landscape itself becomes their weapon. Brutal, close-quarters fighting in chest-high water. Beat: climax of violence.

chapters.title: The Ledger Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. During the battle's chaos, Ilse executes the plan: photographs of the ledger's key pages transmitted via satellite uplink to journalists, archivists, and—crucially—to every district office simultaneously, making suppression impossible. Kessler's leverage dies in the open air. Beat: climax of idea over force.

chapters.title: Kessler's Last Contract
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Cornered and ruined, Kessler offers Rafael everything—reinstatement, wealth, the erasure of his brother's case file—in exchange for the original ledger. Rafael refuses, and Kessler, seeing himself clearly for the first time, surrenders rather than drown for it. Beat: villain's fall without melodrama.

chapters.title: After the Water
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Flood recedes. Investigations begin; the forged deeds unravel publicly; the councils file claims no one can now dismiss. Rafael burns his ranger commission in a tin drum, symbolically ending the decade of measured miles. Ilse receives a job offer anywhere in the world. Beat: release and choice.

chapters.title: Staying
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael asks Ilse not to leave with him but to stay with him—here, in the basin, helping the councils rebuild their water records honestly. She says yes. The cave has closed beneath the tide again, its cost paid. Beat: love chosen over flight.

chapters.title: The Compass Points Home
chapters.summary: Epilogue, shared POV. One year later: a new survey office on the river, run jointly by the councils, with Rafael mapping boundaries and Ilse guarding the flows. A young tracker arrives chasing a thief, mirroring Rafael's old life. Rafael gives him directions—and advice to measure in years, not miles. Beat: full-circle resolution.
